title: Choose Transkrip’s visual world
question: Keep the signal-room workspace, take an alternate, or ask for a fresh set.

options.label: Signal Room
options.lineage: seismic monitoring rooms and field waveform records
options.thesis: The transcript is a live signal record: every word remains anchored to audible evidence and local machine state.
options.viewport: A narrow secure-workspace rail, a large waveform horizon, and the active transcript aligned beneath the same time axis.
options.risk: Can feel operationally dense if quiet review states are not given enough breathing room.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.lineage: laboratory counters and blackened steel instruments
options.thesis: Local processing becomes a physical count of time, segments, and model work rather than an invisible spinner.
options.case: Strong audience identification, but weaker product clarity: the counters dramatize progress more naturally than transcript review.
options.viewport: A bank of glowing time counters sits above a restrained transcript ledger and transport controls.
options.risk: The physical metaphor can overstate itself and reduce long-form reading comfort.

options.label: Sixteen-Color Field
options.thesis: A fixed-region workstation gives audio, transcript, and actions unmistakable permanent places.
options.case: Excellent product clarity, but weaker enterprise identification: the retro pixel language may read as novelty in formal deployments.
options.viewport: A fixed audio field fills the upper frame while the editable transcript docks in a bordered lower window.
options.risk: Pixel typography and integer scaling can limit density and accessibility.

options.label: Visible Grid
options.thesis: A visible modular grid makes every timestamp, language state, and transcript block feel deliberately constructed.
options.case: High enterprise confidence and clear hierarchy, but fuses less naturally with continuous audio than Signal Room.
options.viewport: A monumental TRANSKRIP wordmark locks into a visible grid above a rigorous two-column processing workspace.
options.risk: The grid can become graphic decoration unless every alignment remains functional.

canonCard.label: The enterprise standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar three-column transcription dashboard, executed with restraint and precision.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional app header, upload panel, waveform card, and transcript editor.
canonCard.risk: Immediately legible, but less distinctive and less able to make on-device processing memorable.
